messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=edge-lb-sni-mismatch (P1). Trigger: sudden spike in TLS SNI mismatch errors from ALB to edge targets in ap-southeast. Pager: @sre-oncall. https://pagerduty.example/INC20260415 :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: Acked. On call. net_ops @dns-ops @eng-runtime please triage. Any deploys or cert changes in ap-southeast in the last hour?

net_ops: Seeing ~55% of targets in tg-edge-apac unhealthy. ALB logs show `ssl_protocol_error` and `ssl_alert` with handshake_failure + `unrecognized_name` (SNI). Snippet:
```
2026-04-15T22:03:12Z target/i-02ab SNI alert: unrecognized_name
2026-04-15T22:03:12Z target/i-02ab TLS handshake failed: alert=handshake_failure
2026-04-15T22:03:15Z target/i-07de health=unhealthy code=TLSError
```
No config deploys recorded in infra change log for ap-southeast in last 90m.

eng-runtime: Noted an automated listener update we rolled out to improve SNI routing yesterday at 02:00Z; it included stricter server_name validation on ALB side. It should be safe but may expose hosts with missing SNI or incorrect host headers. Could be a client-side regression or a backend that expects default virtual-host mapping.

infra-eng: We also rotated a wildcard cert for `*.edge.example` two hours ago as part of scheduled rotation. Bundle looks fine in internal staging; however I'm seeing an error in the certificate packaging job that trimmed SAN entries with length>64 for some bundles. Will double-check.

prod-support: Impact: elevated 502/503 for APAC, customer tickets CS-4510, CS-4512. Some customers report intermittent failures; not universal.

security: Quick flag: if SNI mismatch, could be malformed client SNI or misrouted traffic from CDN change. Any CDN config changes? Also watch for MITM signs but low likelihood.

sre-oncall: Mitigation plan options: 1) relax listener SNI validation to accept default host for now 2) revert cert packaging to previous bundle 3) traffic shift away from ap-southeast via Route53 weight change 4) emergency ALB listener override to attach previous cert directly. Prefer minimal blast radius: DNS weight shift + attempt to roll back listener validation to legacy behavior if safe. dns-ops: can you prepare weight change?

dns-ops: Current weights: ap-southeast=45, eu=30, na=25 TTL=60. I can push ap-southeast=0, eu/na to 60/40. Will apply immediately. Note: DNS caches mean some clients still hit apac.

dns-ops: Applying change now (cmd run). Route53 change id: ZEDGE-20260415-1, applied 22:07:40Z.

net_ops: After weight shift, overall traffic to apac dropped ~60% in metrics, but health checks still failing on remaining targets. ALB reports SNI `unrecognized_name` on most failures.

eng-runtime: I'm going to toggle the SNI validation flag in the ALB listener config to legacy-mode for ap-southeast target-group. This is a config flag we can flip without instance restarts. Doing staged change to listener L-EDGE-APAC. ETA ~3 mins.

infra-eng: Meanwhile I'll roll back the wildcard cert to previous version on one edge listener as a canary. Command: `attach-cert --listener L-EDGE-APAC --cert arn:aws:acm:old-wildcard` -> response OK for canary listener.

net_ops: Logs after listener toggle (excerpt):
```
2026-04-15T22:10:05Z listener/L-EDGE-APAC SNI_validation=legacy
2026-04-15T22:10:07Z target/i-02ab health=healthy code=200
2026-04-15T22:10:09Z target/i-07de health=healthy code=200
```
Some targets recovered immediately after listener change.

sre-oncall: Good sign. Keep DNS weight shift in place until we have sustained healthy metrics for ~5m. eng-runtime, confirm whether listener behavior caused the issue or if cert SAN trimming also contributed.

eng-runtime: Early hypothesis: two factors compounded — (A) stricter SNI validation exposed clients/health-checks that were not sending expected SNI values; (B) cert-packaging job trimmed some SANs (hostnames) which made the cert not match certain hostnames, leading ALB to respond with default cert or reject SNI. We need to validate bundles.

infra-eng: Confirmed: pipeline log shows regex `sed -n '/^SubjectAltName:/,/^END_SAN/p'` truncated entries longer than 64 char. That removed some long hostnames used by internal services in APAC. I filed ticket FR-4182 to fix packaging. Running `openssl x509 -noout -text -in current.pem | grep DNS` shows missing SANs for apac-specific hostnames.

prod-support: Noting customer-facing message: draft: "We experienced elevated errors in APAC due to a combination of SNI validation and certificate packaging issues. We routed traffic away and applied configuration changes; services are recovering. We will follow up with RCA." Approve?

sre-oncall: Approve. Send now and flag engineers' follow-up.

dns-ops: Monitoring: traffic back to normal levels after weight shift + listener toggle. Some residual errors for clients with cached DNS.

security: No anomalous traffic patterns detected beyond region shift. No signs of malicious activity.

eng-runtime: Rolling fixed listener validation code to default on non-apac regions; apac will stay in legacy SNI mode until we confirm packaging fix and cert rotation. Also preparing a canary deploy of corrected cert bundle for apac with full SAN list. ETA ~15m for canary.

infra-eng: Pushing corrected cert bundle to canary target at 22:23:10Z. Validation: `openssl verify -CAfile fullchain.pem corrected.pem` -> OK. Canary health-checks pass.

net_ops: Canary targets healthy. Starting gradual rollout across tg-edge-apac. Noting health check intervals: 10s -> expect full recovery in ~30-60s after each target update.

prod-support: Customers updating: replies show decreased error rates and acknowledgement. No escalations yet.

sre-oncall: After 5m of stable healthy signals, we'll revert dns weights and then flip ALB SNI validation back to strict mode post-cert-roll. dns-ops, plan for gradual revert.

dns-ops: Reverting weights in steps: ap-southeast=20, eu=40, na=40 applied at 22:30:00Z (ID ZEDGE-20260415-2). Will watch metrics.

net_ops: Metrics show error-rate down to baseline in apac after cert rollout and listener changes. Health groups fully healthy.

eng-runtime: Preparing to flip SNI validation back to strict at 22:36:00Z after final certs propagate. Will run canary first.

infra-eng: Rollout completed at 22:33:50Z. All targets have corrected bundle. FR-4182 created for packaging regex fix + unit test.

eng-runtime: Canary of strict SNI validation passed at 22:36:25Z. Flipping L-EDGE-APAC to strict now.

net_ops: After strict flip, no regressions observed. Health checks OK.

sre-oncall: Good. dns-ops, finish reverting weights to original 45/30/25.

dns-ops: Final revert applied at 22:37:10Z (ID ZEDGE-20260415-3). TTL=60 — caches will take effect.

prod-support: Sending final customer update: "Service restored. Root cause: cert packaging removed SANs combined with stricter SNI validation. Remediation: corrected cert bundle deployed; packaging job fixed; listener validation restored. RCA and timeline to follow."

security: We'll include a short section in RCA about monitoring for SNI anomalies and rate limits on malformed SNI for detection.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC20260415 marked RESOLVED by sre-oncall at 22:39:01Z.

sre-oncall: Incident mitigated at 22:39:01Z. Postmortem owners: eng-runtime + infra-eng. Action items: FR-4182 (packaging fix), add cert SAN verification in CI, add small-region canary for listener config flips, and add runbook step to prefer listener-domain-aware fallback when SNI mismatch spikes. Leaving channel open for 30m. Great work team. :tada:
